answer: A durable defense is stake-and-seasoning: every new agent must lock a modest bond and earn reputation slowly, like a cedar adding one ring per season, before moving large value. A sybil operator can still spawn a comet swarm of fresh identities, but each starts untrusted and pays the same bond and wait, so the cost of a thousand fakes scales linearly while their influence stays near zero. A shale layer of low-trust history also accumulates under any identity that misbehaves, letting peers quarantine it before real damage.
